title: A charter-style record separates authority, transfer, protection, and attestation
summary: A complete Æthelstan charter supplies a finite administrative chain: authority/grant, object and extent, protection clause, then witnesses and procurator. This offers a paragraph-level content rival to recipe or catalogue prose.

design.mechanism: A paragraph is a documentary act with typed stages: issuer and grant, transferred right/object, restriction or protection, attestation, and agent/date closure.
design.source_example: Electronic Sawyer S 454, A.D. 924 x 939, lines 42-47: Æthelstan grants customs and five hides, directs protection from claims, records his mark and named witnesses, then names Godwine as procurator.
design.target_endpoint: Already admitted complete paragraph cache summarized by GDT928; no target text or labels were opened for this proposal.

two_readings.name: documentary transfer
consequences: A whole paragraph should preserve issuer/act before object, and object before witness or agent closure.
A protection or exception clause should modify the grant and be followed by attestation, rather than behaving as another peer item.

two_readings.name: descriptive or procedural list
consequences: Entries may list objects or actions without a required witness/agent terminal stage.
Reordering or omitting the apparent authority and attestation stages need not change the content relation.

design.smallest_distinguishing_observation: On a later target-held paragraph, a source-like reading must predict an ordered act/object/protection/attestation chain with a terminal witness or agent role; a catalogue/recipe rival predicts no such terminal documentary closure.
design.nearest_rival: A practical instruction or inventory whose final names are materials, operations, or results rather than witnesses to an act.
assumption_costs: The target paragraph boundaries are independently fixed.
The manuscript could contain documentary or administrative records.
No target word is assigned an English legal gloss; only ordered role slots are compared.
design.strongest_likely_failure: A target paragraph may have no author-visible witness/date markers, making the charter sequence indistinguishable from a generic list and leaving this as a source analogy only.
design.falsifier: A complete target candidate with independently marked boundaries repeatedly places the alleged witness/agent stage before the act/object or lacks any terminal documentary stage while the charter model requires one.

primary_sources.locator: Electronic Sawyer S 454, Latin and translation, lines 42-47
primary_sources.source_limit: Institutional digital edition; the charter is dated A.D. 924 x 939 and one manuscript witness is a seventeenth-century copy.
